facts.title: Christmas Island Was Named on Christmas Day 1643
facts.summary: Christmas Island, an Australian territory in the Indian Ocean, got its name because Captain William Mynors of the East India Company ship Royal Mary sailed past it on Christmas Day 1643.

facts.title: Christmas Trees Had Become Common in America by the 1870s
facts.summary: By the 1870s, putting up a Christmas tree had become common in America, a custom with German roots.

facts.title: Christmas Was Banned in Boston for 22 Years
facts.summary: From 1659 to 1681, celebrating Christmas was an offence in the Massachusetts Bay Colony, which included Boston.

facts.title: Coca-Cola Ads Shaped Santa's Look, but Didn't Invent His Red Suit
facts.summary: In 1931 the illustrator Haddon Sundblom began painting Santa Claus in a red suit for The Coca-Cola Company's Christmas advertising, and he went on painting Santa for the company for the next 33 years.

facts.title: Enemy Soldiers Played Football During the 1914 Christmas Truce
facts.summary: Around Christmas 1914, British and German soldiers on parts of the Western Front stopped fighting, met in no man's land and, in some places, played informal football.

facts.title: Oslo Sends London a Christmas Tree Every Year
facts.summary: Every year since 1947, the city of Oslo has given London a Christmas tree as thanks for British support to Norway during the Second World War.

facts.title: Poinsettias Are Named After a US Diplomat
facts.summary: The poinsettia's English name honors Joel Roberts Poinsett, a US diplomat who served as the first United States minister to Mexico, where the plant grows wild.

facts.title: Sweden's Giant Christmas Goat Keeps Getting Burned Down
facts.summary: Sweden's giant straw Gävle Goat, built for the Christmas season since 1966, has been destroyed or damaged in most years: as of December 2025, 43 of its 60 goats had met that fate.

facts.title: The First Artificial Christmas Trees Were Made of Goose Feathers
facts.summary: Some of the first artificial Christmas trees were made in 19th-century Germany from goose feathers dyed green, partly as a response to continuing deforestation.

facts.title: The First Christmas Card Was Sent in 1843
facts.summary: The first commercial Christmas card was commissioned by Sir Henry Cole in London in 1843 and illustrated by the artist John Callcott Horsley.

facts.title: Tchaikovsky's 'The Nutcracker' Premiered in 1892
facts.summary: Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker premiered on 18 December 1892 at the Imperial Mariinsky Theatre in Saint Petersburg, on a double bill with his opera Iolanta.

facts.title: Tinsel Was Once Made of Real Silver
facts.summary: Tinsel was invented in Nuremberg, Germany, in 1610, and the first versions were made from shredded strands of real silver.

facts.title: Bing Crosby's 'White Christmas' Is the Best-Selling Single of All Time
facts.summary: Bing Crosby's recording of Irving Berlin's "White Christmas" is the best-selling single in history, with an estimated 50 million-plus physical copies sold.

facts.title: 'Xmas' Is Not a Modern Abbreviation
facts.summary: The X in Xmas is not a modern way of crossing Christ out of Christmas.
